title: Tail and inclusive interval probabilities from a demand table
scenario_markdown: Daily emergency-parts demand X takes values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.25, 0.15 respectively. A depot stocks one unit, and also wants to know how often demand lies from one through three inclusive.
assumptions: The PMF sums to one and exhausts all possible daily demands.
The interval includes both endpoints; at least two means X>=2.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is P(X>=2), the probability one stocked unit is insufficient? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: At least two includes demand exactly two.
P(X=2) is only one outcome in the tail.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is P(1<=X<=3)? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: Include the endpoints 1 and 3, not just the interior.
Exclude demand 4 as well as demand 0.
The complement must exclude X=2 from the subtracted event.
The complement of X>=2 includes both 0 and 1.

stages.explanation_markdown: For integer counts, 'at least 2' includes 2. Its complement is 'at most 1'. Subtracting P(X<=2) instead computes P(X>=3), losing the mass at 2.
